23.0.0.en: 1- The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

23.0.1.en: 1- David feels that God has shepherded his life since his existence in the world and continues to shepherd him; He is the constant Shepherd of his life, and not only in a particular time.

23.0.2.en: 2- Christ described Himself as the good Shepherd, so the words of the Psalm apply to Christ as the Shepherd of our souls, and at the same time Christ became a Lamb by His Incarnation, to be the firstborn among many brethren, so that He speaks with us, saying that the Lord is shepherd; and every believer sees the fatherhood of God in His being the Shepherd of his life.

23.0.3.en: 3- People in the East were accustomed to call good kings shepherds, because they care for their peoples and show fatherhood toward them.

23.0.4.en: 4- The shepherd provides for his flock all its needs, so that it lacks nothing; so too David found no title to express God's care and His sufficiency for the needs of His children except the title of Shepherd.

23.0.5.en: 5- The more a person trusts in God and empties his own will, the more he feels God's sufficiency for him, and even in tribulations he sees them as for his good, and sees God's nearness to him, so he is not troubled and is assured that He will arrange all his needs for him.

23.1.0.en: 2- He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me to the waters of rest.

23.1.1.en: He maketh me to lie down: He makes me sit; for the sheep fold their legs and settle on the ground to rest.

23.1.2.en: He leadeth me: He brings me to the watering places that I may drink.

23.1.3.en: 1- The flock eats of the green pastures and rests in them, secure because of the food available in them, and these green pastures are:

23.1.4.en: a - The Eucharist, which satisfies God's children, and as they are always bound to it, they remain in continual fullness.

23.1.5.en: b - The word of God, which nourishes souls.

23.1.6.en: c - Christ, in whom the soul settles and finds its fullness.

23.1.7.en: d - The Church, which satisfies her children with her teachings, her rites, her hymns and her praises.

23.1.8.en: 2- After the flock has eaten it needs to drink; therefore the shepherd leads it to the waters of rest, for the sheep cannot go to the water except under the shepherd's leadership. Likewise it is easier for sheep to drink from still water than from running water, so the water of rest is better for the sheep. And the waters of rest are:

23.1.9.en: a - The work of the Holy Spirit in the soul.

23.1.11.en: c - The work of grace, which is given freely to man for his need.

23.1.12.en: d - The waters of rest are the waters of the Holy Spirit, of which whoever drinks will never thirst, as Christ said to the Samaritan woman (Jn 4:13, 14), because everyone who drinks of the waters of the world will thirst again.

23.1.13.en: 3- Water washes away dirt, and likewise the waters of the Holy Spirit cleanse man from every sin.

23.1.14.en: 4- Water extinguishes fire and cools heat; so too the waters of the Holy Spirit extinguish the fire of lusts.

23.1.15.en: 5- Water irrigates the earth so that it gives fruit; likewise the waters of the Holy Spirit give the fruits of the virtues.

23.1.16.en: Look to God your Shepherd, who is able to supply all your needs, so that you are not troubled by any tribulation, even if all the people around you are troubled.

23.2.0.en: 3- He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.

23.2.1.en: 1- I am liable to be distracted from my Shepherd and to go astray in paths far from Him. But His love does not leave me, so He brings me back from my straying and I walk with the rest of the flock, that is, I return to His Church and His worship and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him. He is not angry with me and does not leave me because of my evils, but His love forgives me and brings me back to life with Him.

23.2.2.en: 2- If I am enjoying the green pastures in which I lie down, but in my ignorance I walk in the way of lusts, that is, the barren wilderness full of thorns, I am wounded by the thorns of sin; but my God guides me in the paths of righteousness, which are holiness, goodness, the virtues and doing good.

23.2.3.en: 3- Christ is the way, the truth and the life, so the paths of righteousness are Christ; that is, He guides me to Himself, because all my straying is a choice of the lusts of the world instead of Christ, and guidance is the return to His beloved Person.

23.2.4.en: 4- Christ, who guides me to Himself, does this not because of my worthiness but by His love, for the glorification of His holy name.

23.3.0.en: 4- Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

23.3.1.en: 1- The valley of the shadow of death is trials and tribulations. It is not the valley of death but its shadow; that is, a person feels that he is almost dying, that is, the tribulation is very severe, but the sense of God's being with me reassures my heart, so I do not fear any troubles.

23.3.2.en: 2- The shadow of death signifies bodily death, while by true death is meant spiritual death, that is, eternal perdition. Therefore the meaning of the verse is that during our life in the world until its end in death we fear no evil, because God is with us; indeed bodily death leads to a release into eternal life.

23.3.3.en: 3- The sense that God is with me not only reassures my heart but comforts it and makes it patient in sufferings, and more than this, as I feel God's love I rejoice and taste the Kingdom while I am on earth.

23.3.4.en: 4- God's presence with me makes me fear Him, and then I keep away from every sin and do not fear it, nor people, nor problems and the changes of life.

23.3.5.en: 5- The rod and the staff signify the Cross, since both are made of wood, and the shepherd uses them in his hand to shepherd his flock and take care of it.

23.3.6.en: 6- The rod protects the flock by gathering the straying and striking the wolves and all the enemies of the flock, so it is protection from Satan and all his tricks and violence.

23.3.7.en: 7- The shepherd leans on the staff, and it signifies divine support in the spiritual life, so that even if a person is weak, by leaning on the staff he continues his way toward the Kingdom and acquires the virtues.

23.3.8.en: 8- The shepherd uses the rod and the staff to lead his flock, that is, by looking to the Cross we reject all evil, and offer our lives in self-giving love and find our salvation. In short, we find in the Cross all that we desire, and in the end it gives us comfort and joy.

23.3.9.en: 9- The thickness of the rod of discipline varies according to the sheep's endurance; it is slender to suit the weak sheep, and thick for the stubborn and arrogant. In addition, the rod can turn into a staff and the staff into a rod according to need. The weak needs support, while the careless and stubborn needs discipline until he repents.

23.3.10.en: 10- The staff is useful in old age; so too in spiritual old age and lukewarmness God supports with His grace.

23.3.11.en: 11- The staff is useful if a person walks in darkness, for it guides him to the road and protects him from dangers. So too when consolations disappear and God hides Himself, even for a little while, we lean on the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace, and they guide us to the way of the Kingdom.

23.3.12.en: 12- The rod is for discipline and the staff for support and help, but both are in the hand of God the Father, the tender Shepherd of our souls, who uses them for our salvation; they comfort us, that is, they give inner peace, and then the Kingdom of Heaven.

23.3.13.en: God loves you and is ready to lead your life, so surrender yourself to Him, because His will is your salvation, whether He allows you a tribulation or gives you support; but in the end you are in a faithful hand that brings you to the Kingdom.

23.4.0.en: 5- Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of them that trouble me: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup is full.

23.4.2.en: 1- The table is the altar of the New Testament, where the Body and Blood of the Lord are offered, and it satisfies the souls of believers. And God offers it to His children and sets it before them every day, that they may be satisfied with His love.

23.4.3.en: 2- The table is also my bodily needs, which God arranges for me as long as I am occupied with seeking the Kingdom, so I am not troubled about any need, because God shepherds me and satisfies me materially and spiritually.

23.4.4.en: 3- God's arrangement of my spiritual and material needs is in front of those who trouble me, that is, my enemies the demons, so I do not fear them, because God is with me, and He declares His support for me at a table over which Satan has no authority. And he cannot take away my peace and my sufficiency, because they are from God.

23.4.5.en: 4- The table is one, which is the altar of the New Testament, which Solomon's Temple and the Tabernacle of Meeting signified. And the Body and Blood of the Lord are offered on this table in every place to everyone who believes in Him.

23.4.6.en: 5- The anointing of the head with oil is a clear reference to the sacrament of the Holy Myron and the descent of the Holy Spirit, which begins with the anointing of the head, which is very important because it contains the mind, and then extends to anoint the rest of the members.

23.4.7.en: 6- Priests, prophets and kings were anointed with oil by its being poured on their heads, and it is a reference to the sacrament of the priesthood in the New Testament, where the Holy Spirit anoints them, to lead the Church and perform the Holy Sacraments.

23.4.8.en: 7- It was the custom in ancient times to place oil and perfume on the table, so that the guest would be anointed with them. And the anointing of the head signifies joy, for the one who fasts, as Christ commanded, anoints his head, to hide his asceticism and express his spiritual joy. And the host used to pour oil on the heads of the guests, as Christ mentioned in the house of Simon the Pharisee when He met the sinful woman. So anointing the head with oil represents honor, and offering love to others so that their souls rejoice.

23.4.9.en: 8- Anointing with ointment or oil was used in ancient times to treat and soothe wounds, and God wants to heal our pains and remove our sins from us; He heals the diseases of our souls and bodies by His Holy Spirit, as happens in the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.

23.4.10.en: 9- The cup is the cup of Christ's blood on the table of the New Testament, which waters the souls of believers completely, so that they do not need the waters of the world, that is, they rise above earthly things and are not troubled by their changes.

23.4.11.en: 10- In ancient times shepherds used to fill large cups made of stone, into which they put water from the springs, so that the sheep might drink from the cups, and they kept pouring water into the cups so that it would be cold; and this signifies the renewal of the work of the Holy Spirit in souls, for He gives them coolness, peace and gifts renewed every day.

23.4.12.en: 11- The cup signifies the cup of wine that gladdens whoever drinks it, and this signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who makes the soul drunk with the love of God, so it rejoices and forgets the material things around it, that is, it rises above material things and is occupied with divine love.

23.5.0.en: 6- Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

23.5.1.en: 1- If a person walks in the way of God, as the verses of this Psalm mention, then in the end God grants him goodness and mercy all the days of his life, that is, He forgives him his sins, finds excuses for him, and blesses him with many good things.

23.5.2.en: 2- Goodness and mercy are perfected in the Person of Christ; that is, whoever lives with Christ, Christ rejoices in him and seeks him and fills his heart. Christ follows him, overtakes him, and dwells in him throughout his life, because this person declared his love and submission to God.

23.5.3.en: 3- Christ grants the one who loves Him and responds to Him to dwell and settle in His house throughout the days of his life; for although this person has a private dwelling and a job, the time he spends in the house of the Lord is the delight of his life, and his heart clings to the Church and her teachings and settles in her, so that he is satisfied and enlightened, and becomes a light to the world in every place he goes to. In ancient times they used to pray the prayer of the Prime in the church and then go to their work, and when they returned from their work they prayed the prayer of the Vespers in the church; that is, they began the day with the blessing of the Church and ended it by standing before God and being satisfied with His love, to return joyfully to their homes.

23.5.4.en: The Church is the house of God your heavenly Father, who rejoices to see you in His house and blesses you. So cling to the Church and all that is in her as much as you can, and you will receive unspeakable grace and blessing. God the King of Glory. Of David. A Psalm: "The earth is the LORD'S, and the fulness thereof" (v. 1). Introduction:

23.5.7.en: David the prophet said it when he brought up the ark of the covenant of God from the house of Obededom to Jerusalem (2 Sam 6:12-17).

23.5.8.en: 3- David wrote it by the spirit of prophecy about the founding of Solomon's Temple, to be said when the ark is brought up to it.

23.5.9.en: 4- It is said on returning from any victory in war with the enemies.

23.5.10.en: 5- There is a relationship between Psalms 22, 23 and 24. The first speaks about Christ the Savior, the second about Christ the Shepherd, and the third about Christ the Glorified. These three Psalms also represent the hymn of Golgotha, then the hymn of the redeemed Church, and after this the hymn of heaven.

23.5.11.en: 6- This Psalm is messianic, speaking about Christ ascending to heaven in order to raise us up with Him; therefore this Psalm is said in the rite of the New Testament Church on the Feasts of the Resurrection and the Ascension.

23.5.12.en: 7- The title of this Psalm in the Septuagint is "for the first day of the week", because this Psalm used to be recited on the day after the Sabbath, that is, Sunday, which is the first day of the week. And this represents in the New Testament the day of the Resurrection, on which Christ rose, triumphant over death.

23.5.13.en: 8- The manner of reciting this Psalm in the Old Testament was that those entering the Temple say (vv. 1, 2) all together with one voice, to proclaim the power of God, the Creator of the whole universe. After this the leader of the group entering the Temple says the third verse, asking about the conditions of the one who enters the house of God. After this the gatekeeper answers from inside the house of the Lord, declaring the conditions of the one who enters the house of the Lord, which are the two verses (vv. 4, 5). After this the leader of the group outside the house of the Lord says the sixth verse, declaring the blessings of the one who enters the house of the Lord, then continues and asks the guards to open the gates for the King of Glory, and recites the seventh verse.

23.5.14.en: The guard inside the house asks who the King of Glory is, in the eighth verse. The leader of the group from outside replies, declaring His attributes in the ninth verse.

23.5.15.en: The gatekeeper returns from inside and asks the same question, that is, who the King of Glory is, in the first part of the tenth verse.

23.5.16.en: The Church in the New Testament took up this rite, and recites part of it on the Feast of the Resurrection and calls it the play of the Resurrection, reciting verses (7-10).

23.5.17.en: 9- This Psalm is found in the Third Hour in the Agpeya, in which we celebrate the descent of the Holy Spirit, because the seas and the rivers in (v. 2) signify Baptism, and the Psalm also shows the work of the Holy Spirit in those entering the house of the Lord.
